newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia upgrades refinery to cover gasoline needs.
newsitem.headline: Colombia upgrades refinery to cover gasoline needs.

text.p: Colombia is aiming to become self-sufficient in gasoline within the next three years with a multi-million dollar investment to upgrade part of the country's biggest refinery, the state oil company Ecopetrol said Monday.
Ecopetrol said it will spend $75 million modernizing equipment used to process sweet crudes at its Barrancabermeja plant, which has a total throughput of about 230,000 barrels per day (bpd).
The first phase of the project will involve installing a topping, at a cost of about $18 million, that will boost throughput by 40,000 bpd.

An Ecopetrol spokesman said almost all of that will be sweet crude from the Cusiana field which the state oil company operates in association with multinational British Petroleum Co Plc and its partners.

"This project aims to boost production levels and enable the refinery to handle better quality crudes which will enable us to cover national gasoline demand," Pedro Rizo, head of the Barrancabermeja refinery, told the leading El Tiempo newspaper.
Colombia currently has a 30,000 bpd shortfall in gasoline.
